meaning: A tall container with a scale, used to measure the volume of a liquid.
example: Read the volume at the bottom of the meniscus in the measuring cylinder.

meaning: A quantity that has size only, with no direction, such as mass or speed.
example: Speed is a scalar, but velocity is not.

meaning: A quantity that has both size and direction, such as force or velocity.
example: Force is a vector, so its direction matters.

meaning: The distance travelled per unit time.
example: The speed of the train is 30 m/s.

meaning: How far something travels.

meaning: Not changing.

meaning: Not moving.

meaning: The constant speed reached by a falling object when the air resistance equals its weight.

meaning: A measure of the quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms.

meaning: The gravitational force on an object that has mass, measured in newtons.
example: An astronaut’s weight is smaller on the Moon than on the Earth.

meaning: The force per unit mass on an object in a gravitational field.
example: The gravitational field strength on the Earth is about 9.8 N/kg.

meaning: The mass per unit volume of a substance.
example: Gold has a much higher density than water.

meaning: The amount of space that something takes up.
example: The volume of the stone is 20 cm³.

meaning: To stay on the surface of a liquid without sinking.
example: Ice floats because it is less dense than water.

meaning: A push or a pull, measured in newtons.
example: A force can change the speed, direction or shape of an object.

meaning: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting on an object.
example: When the forces are balanced, the resultant force is zero.

meaning: A force that acts against the motion of a surface sliding over another surface.
example: Friction between the tyres and the road stops the car from skidding.

meaning: The force from the air that acts against an object moving through it.
example: A parachute increases the air resistance on a skydiver.

meaning: The increase in length of a spring when a load stretches it.
example: The extension of the spring is 4 cm when the load is 2 N.

meaning: The point beyond which the extension of a spring is no longer proportional to the load.
example: After the limit of proportionality, the load–extension graph starts to curve.

meaning: The turning effect of a force about a pivot.
example: A longer spanner gives a bigger moment for the same force.

meaning: The fixed point that something turns around.
example: The seesaw balances on a pivot in the middle.

meaning: The state of an object when there is no resultant force and no resultant moment on it.
example: The beam is in equilibrium, so the clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal.

meaning: The point through which the whole weight of an object seems to act.
example: A bus with a low centre of gravity is hard to tip over.

meaning: Not easily knocked over.
example: A wide base makes a lamp more stable.

meaning: The mass of an object multiplied by its velocity.
example: A heavy lorry has a lot of momentum even at a low speed.

meaning: The force on an object multiplied by the time for which the force acts.
example: A crumple zone reduces the force by making the impulse last longer.

meaning: An event in which two moving objects hit each other.
example: Total momentum is the same before and after the collision.

meaning: Something that is stored and transferred when things happen, measured in joules.
example: A battery stores energy in a chemical store.

meaning: The energy an object has because it is moving.
example: The kinetic energy of the car increases as it speeds up.

meaning: The energy an object has because of its height in a gravitational field.
example: A book on a high shelf has more gravitational potential energy than one on the floor.

meaning: Energy stored in fuels, food and batteries.
example: Food is a store of chemical energy.

meaning: Energy stored in an object that is stretched or squashed, such as a spring.
example: A stretched catapult stores elastic energy.

meaning: The total energy of the particles in an object.
example: Heating the water increases its internal energy.

meaning: The principle that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred from one store to another.
example: By the conservation of energy, the total energy before and after is the same.

meaning: The energy transferred when a force moves an object.
example: The work done lifting the box is 50 J.

meaning: The work done or energy transferred per unit time.
example: A kettle with a higher power boils water faster.

meaning: The useful energy output as a percentage of the total energy input.
example: An LED lamp has a higher efficiency than a filament lamp.

meaning: Able to be replaced naturally, so it will not run out.
example: Wind and solar power are renewable energy resources.

meaning: Not able to be replaced once it has been used, so it will run out.
example: Coal is a non-renewable energy resource.

meaning: A fuel such as coal, oil or natural gas, formed from the remains of living things millions of years ago.
example: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide.

meaning: The splitting of a large nucleus into two smaller nuclei, which releases energy.
example: Nuclear power stations use nuclear fission of uranium.

meaning: The joining of two small nuclei to form a larger nucleus, which releases energy.
example: The Sun releases energy by nuclear fusion.

meaning: The force per unit area.
example: A sharp knife cuts well because it puts a high pressure on the food.

meaning: A very small piece of matter, such as an atom or a molecule.
example: The particles in a gas move quickly in all directions.

meaning: Without any pattern or order.
example: Gas particles move in random directions.

meaning: The lowest possible temperature, 0 K (about −273 °C), at which particles have the least kinetic energy.
example: Nothing can be cooled below absolute zero.

meaning: The change from a solid to a liquid.
example: During melting, the temperature of the ice stays at 0 °C.

meaning: The change from a liquid to a gas at a fixed temperature, with bubbles forming inside the liquid.
example: Pure water starts boiling at 100 °C at sea level.

meaning: The escape of more-energetic particles from the surface of a liquid.
example: Evaporation cools the skin when sweat dries.

meaning: The change from a gas to a liquid.
example: Condensation forms drops of water on a cold window.

meaning: The change from a liquid to a solid.
example: Solidification of water happens at 0 °C.

meaning: The increase in size of a material when it is heated.
example: Gaps are left between rails to allow for thermal expansion.

meaning: The energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C.
example: Water has a high specific heat capacity, so it heats up slowly.

meaning: The transfer of thermal energy through a material without the material itself moving.
example: A metal spoon in hot soup gets hot by conduction.

meaning: The transfer of thermal energy by the movement of a liquid or a gas.
example: Convection carries warm air to the top of a room.

meaning: The transfer of thermal energy by infrared waves, which needs no material.
example: The Sun warms the Earth by thermal radiation.

meaning: A material that lets thermal energy or electric charge pass through it easily.
example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.

meaning: A material that does not let thermal energy or electric charge pass through it easily.
example: Plastic is used as an insulator around electrical wires.

meaning: A liquid or a gas.
example: Convection can only happen in a fluid.

meaning: Describes a wave in which the vibrations are at right angles to the direction the wave travels.
example: Light waves are transverse.

meaning: Describes a wave in which the vibrations are along the direction the wave travels.
example: Sound waves are longitudinal.

meaning: The greatest distance a point on a wave moves from its rest position.
example: A louder sound has a bigger amplitude.

meaning: The distance from a point on one wave to the same point on the next wave.
example: Radio waves have a much longer wavelength than light.

meaning: The number of waves passing a point each second, measured in hertz.
example: A high-pitched sound has a high frequency.

meaning: The highest point of a wave.
example: The wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next.

meaning: The lowest point of a wave.
example: The boat sank into the trough between two waves.

meaning: The spreading out of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an edge.
example: Diffraction is greatest when the gap is about the same size as the wavelength.

meaning: The bouncing back of a wave from a surface.
example: A mirror forms an image by reflection.

meaning: The change in direction of a wave when it passes from one material into another and its speed changes.
example: Refraction makes a straw in water look bent.

meaning: A line drawn at right angles to a surface at the point where a ray meets it.
example: Measure the angle of incidence from the normal, not from the surface.

meaning: The angle between the ray hitting a surface and the normal.
example: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

meaning: The complete reflection of light back into a material when it hits the boundary at more than the critical angle.
example: Optical fibres carry light by total internal reflection.

meaning: The angle of incidence above which light is totally internally reflected.
example: The critical angle for glass is about 42°.

meaning: A lens that is thicker in the middle and brings parallel rays of light together at a point.
example: A magnifying glass is a converging lens.

meaning: The distance from the centre of a lens to its principal focus.
example: A thicker lens has a shorter focal length.

meaning: The splitting of white light into its colours.
example: A prism shows the dispersion of white light into a spectrum.

meaning: A quick movement backwards and forwards.
example: Sound is made by the vibration of an object.

meaning: A sound that is heard again after it reflects off a surface.
example: The bat finds insects by listening for the echo.

meaning: How high or low a sound is.
example: A sound with a higher frequency has a higher pitch.

meaning: Sound with a frequency above 20 000 Hz, too high for humans to hear.
example: Doctors use ultrasound to see a baby before it is born.

meaning: One of the two ends of a magnet, where the magnetic force is strongest.
example: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

meaning: The region around a magnet where a magnetic material feels a force.
example: Iron filings show the shape of the magnetic field.

meaning: To pull towards.
example: The north pole of one magnet attracts the south pole of another.

meaning: To push away.
example: Two north poles repel each other.

meaning: A property of particles such as protons and electrons that makes them attract or repel; it can be positive or negative.
example: Rubbing a balloon gives it a negative charge.

meaning: A tiny particle with a negative charge, found outside the nucleus of an atom.
example: When the balloon is rubbed, electrons move onto it.

meaning: The flow of charge around a circuit, measured in amperes.
example: The current in the lamp is 0.5 A.

meaning: The energy transferred per unit charge between two points in a circuit, measured in volts.
example: The potential difference across the lamp is 6 V.

meaning: The energy that a source such as a cell gives to each unit of charge, measured in volts.
example: A cell with an electromotive force of 1.5 V is connected to the lamp.

meaning: How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms.
example: A longer wire has a greater resistance.

meaning: A meter that measures current; it is connected in series.
example: Connect the ammeter in series with the lamp.

meaning: A meter that measures potential difference; it is connected in parallel.
example: Connect the voltmeter in parallel with the resistor.

meaning: Connected one after another, in a single loop.
example: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point.

meaning: Connected in separate branches, side by side.
example: The lamps in a house are connected in parallel.

meaning: One part of a circuit, such as a lamp, a resistor or a switch.
example: Each component in the circuit has its own symbol.

meaning: A resistor whose resistance decreases as its temperature increases.
example: A thermistor is used in a fire alarm circuit.

meaning: A resistor whose resistance decreases as the light on it gets brighter.
example: A light-dependent resistor switches on the street lamp when it gets dark.

meaning: A component that lets current flow in one direction only.
example: The diode stops the current from flowing the wrong way.

meaning: A thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit if the current is too high.
example: The fuse melted when the kettle developed a fault.

meaning: The wire that safely carries current to the ground if a fault makes the metal case of an appliance live.
example: The earth wire is connected to the metal case of the toaster.

meaning: A switch that cuts off the current automatically when it is too high.
example: Unlike a fuse, a circuit breaker can be reset.

meaning: The production of an e.m.f. in a conductor when it moves across a magnetic field, or when the magnetic field around it changes.
example: A bicycle dynamo works by electromagnetic induction.

meaning: A current that keeps changing direction.
example: The mains supply in a house is alternating current.

meaning: A current that flows in one direction only.
example: A battery gives direct current.

meaning: A device that changes the voltage of an alternating current.
example: A transformer steps up the voltage before electricity is sent along power lines.

meaning: A wire wound round into many turns.
example: Moving a magnet into the coil induces a current.

meaning: A machine that produces a voltage by turning a coil in a magnetic field.
example: A wind turbine turns a generator.

meaning: A coil of wire, often around an iron core, that becomes a magnet when a current flows in it.
example: A scrapyard crane uses an electromagnet to lift cars.

meaning: The tiny, positively charged centre of an atom, made of protons and neutrons.
example: Almost all the mass of an atom is in its nucleus.

meaning: A particle with a positive charge, found in the nucleus.
example: A carbon nucleus contains six protons.

meaning: A particle with no charge, found in the nucleus.
example: Carbon-14 has two more neutrons than carbon-12.

meaning: The number of protons in a nucleus.
example: Every oxygen nucleus has a proton number of 8.

meaning: The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus.
example: Uranium-238 has a nucleon number of 238.

meaning: One of two or more forms of an element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
example: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.

meaning: Giving out radiation from unstable nuclei.
example: Radon is a radioactive gas.

meaning: The radiation that is around us all the time, from natural and artificial sources.
example: Rocks and cosmic rays are sources of background radiation.

meaning: A particle of two protons and two neutrons given out by a nucleus; a helium nucleus.
example: An alpha particle is stopped by a sheet of paper.

meaning: A fast-moving electron given out by a nucleus.
example: A beta particle can pass through paper but not through thick aluminium.

meaning: High-frequency electromagnetic radiation given out by a nucleus.
example: A gamma ray can pass through several centimetres of lead.

meaning: Able to knock electrons off atoms, turning them into ions.
example: Alpha radiation is the most strongly ionising.

meaning: The time taken for half the nuclei in a sample of a radioactive isotope to decay.
example: The half-life of iodine-131 is about 8 days.

meaning: The change of an unstable nucleus into a different nucleus, giving out radiation.
example: During alpha decay, the nucleus loses two protons and two neutrons.

meaning: The path of an object moving around a star, planet or moon.
example: The Earth takes one year to complete its orbit of the Sun.

meaning: The imaginary line through the Earth from pole to pole, around which it spins.
example: The Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours.

meaning: The Sun and all the objects that orbit it, such as planets, moons and comets.
example: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.

meaning: A small body of ice and dust that orbits the Sun in a long, oval path.
example: A comet moves fastest when it is closest to the Sun.

meaning: The distance that light travels through space in one year.
example: The nearest star after the Sun is about 4 light-years away.

meaning: A huge group of many billions of stars.
example: The Sun is one of the stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

meaning: An increase in the wavelength of light from a galaxy that is moving away from us.
example: The redshift of distant galaxies shows that the Universe is expanding.
